actions.label: Compare elevated and standard FancyZones shortcut handling

reproduce.title: Verify Win+Arrow behavior after focus changes
prerequisites: FancyZones enabled with at least two zones; one affected window and a second window for focus changes.
steps: Run PowerToys as a standard user, focus and refocus the affected window by Alt+Tab and clicking, then press Win+Left/Right repeatedly.
Repeat the identical sequence with PowerToys elevated.
Compare with the reported Windows-key remapping workaround disabled and enabled; note whether native snapping or FancyZones receives each press.
reproduce.expected_result: The trigger and elevation/remapping dependency are reproducible and the handler responsible for the first snap is identified.

actions.label: Review interception fix direction after reproduction
actions.note: Approve a code-level design only after the elevated/standard comparison identifies the responsible input path.

confidence.rationale: The issue is independently corroborated with a repeatable focus trigger and workaround.

judgment.rationale: The added elevation workaround narrows the next reproduction: compare elevated and standard PowerToys under the same focused-window and left-Win shortcut sequence. Existing focus-change reproductions still support a real issue, but the input-hook or integrity-level cause is not established.
evidence: Several commenters independently reproduce Win+Arrow invoking Windows half-screen snapping before FancyZones movement after focus changes.
The latest reporter says running PowerToys as administrator resolves the symptom; the report does not yet establish whether elevation alone is causal or whether the shortcut/focus conditions changed.
A Windows-key remapping workaround was also reported; no linked fix is present and the issue remains unassigned.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the same Win+Arrow focus sequence with PowerToys elevated and standard, and compare the left-Win key with the reported remapping workaround.

fix_assessment.rationale: The reproduced focus condition and elevation workaround justify a narrow investigation, but do not yet establish the failing input path.

proposed_fixes.title: Preserve FancyZones Win+Arrow handling after focus changes
proposed_fixes.root_cause: A low-confidence hypothesis is that shortcut interception differs after focus changes or between standard and elevated PowerToys processes.
plan: Reproduce the same window-focus changes and Win+Arrow sequence with standard and elevated PowerToys.
Compare left-Win behavior with the reported remapping workaround and capture which process handles the shortcut.
Only after confirming a PowerToys-owned interception gap, make the smallest targeted change and add regression coverage for the focus/elevation boundary.
verification: Win+Arrow consistently advances FancyZones zones after focus changes in the affected launch mode.

Native Windows half-screen snapping and unaffected shortcut behavior remain intact.
